1.explanation:
1. We create an `externalValues` object and pass it into Field’s constructor using the `values` option.  
2. Inside Field’s code, `this.values = options.values || {}` takes a direct reference to that object.  
3. When you call `init('name', { initValue: ... })` or later `setValue('name', ...)`, Field writes to its `this.values` map. Because `this.values` points at your `externalValues`, you’ll see your original object mutated.  
4. The console logs before and after demonstrate that the object you passed into Field has been changed.  

This reproduces the bug: Field should clone the incoming `values` instead of holding a direct reference, to avoid side-effects on user data.
1.bug_scenario: When you pass an object into Field’s constructor via the `values` option, Field will hold a direct reference to that same object (see line 35: `this.values = options.values || {}`), and then when you call `init` (with `initValue`) or `setValue`, Field writes directly into `this.values`—thus mutating your original object. In other words, Field does not clone the incoming `values` object, so any updates you make through Field will also update the object you passed in.
